cultivar: Chinary and clonal bushes of the Darjeeling type
processing: Orthodox black tea made in flushes like Darjeeling: a long wither, gentle rolling, partial oxidation for the spring teas and fuller oxidation in summer and autumn, then firing; certified organic.
harvest_season: March to November in flushes; the first (March–April) and second (May–June) flushes are prized, autumn lots are softer and cheaper.
appearance_dry: Twisted leaf in olive, brown and silver, like a Darjeeling.
taste_profile: Floral and fruity with a honeyed sweetness and a brisk finish; often a little softer and cleaner than a Darjeeling from the same season.

brewing.notes: Brew like a Darjeeling: just under 90 °C, no milk, a second steep for a good lot.

vintage_note: Sold by flush and year under the 'Temi Tea' name, through the garden's own outlets, Indian retailers and the auction system, with first flush on sale from April and second flush from July; grades follow the Darjeeling codes (FTGFOP1 and so on). A few speciality importers carry it abroad. Best within a year of picking.
description:
Temi is the first and largest tea garden of Sikkim, the small Himalayan state between Darjeeling and Bhutan, and its tea is close kin to Darjeeling made just across the border: Chinary and clonal bushes, the flush system, the light spring style, grown on Tendong Hill above Namchi. The garden was founded in 1969 under the last Chogyal (king) of Sikkim and is still run by the state government.

Manufacture is orthodox: a long wither, gentle rolling, partial oxidation for the spring teas and fuller oxidation in summer and autumn, then firing. The garden is certified organic and markets itself heavily on that.

The cup is bright gold to amber, floral and fruity with a honeyed sweetness and a brisk finish, often a little softer and cleaner than a Darjeeling from the same season. Brew it like a Darjeeling: water around 90 °C, three to four minutes, no milk, a second steep for a good lot.

It is sold by flush and year under the 'Temi Tea' name, much of it through the Kolkata auction and the rest packed for local sale, with first flush on sale from April and second flush from July; a few speciality importers carry it abroad. Grades follow the Darjeeling codes (FTGFOP1 and so on). Drink it within a year of picking.

It is a good choice if you want Darjeeling character from a different hillside, and a nice answer to the question of whether the Darjeeling name is about the place or the style.
history:
Tea in Sikkim is essentially the story of one garden. Temi was founded in 1969 by Palden Thondup Namgyal, the last king of Sikkim, as a source of work for the many Tibetan refugees living in the region. It remains the oldest and largest garden in the state, runs to about 440 acres on Tendong Hill and is owned by the state government.

A few small growers have appeared since, such as the boutique Bermiok garden, founded in 2002. Organic certification, recognised for Temi in 2017, has helped raise the tea's profile. About three quarters of Sikkim's crop goes through the Kolkata auction, and first-flush Temi from 2023 sold at Rs 10,250 per kg to buyers in Italy and Korea. Unlike Darjeeling, Sikkim tea has no GI tag.
